name: DC barrel jack (coaxial power)
family: coaxial DC power (center pin + outer sleeve)
ascii:
outer sleeve                center pin
         |                           |
   ======[===========================(o)===>   (insert ->)
         |                           |
       barrel                       tip
     (usually -)                (usually +)
description: The coaxial DC power connector on countless wall-warts and devices. Two conductors: the center pin (tip) and the outer sleeve (barrel). Polarity is a convention, not guaranteed -- most modern gear is center-positive, marked with the center-plus symbol, but always check. The very common size is 5.5 mm outer / 2.1 mm inner (also 2.5 mm inner).

contacts.name: CENTER
contacts.description: center pin -- USUALLY positive (+) on modern center-positive supplies. 2.1 mm or 2.5 mm inner diameter

contacts.name: BARREL
contacts.description: outer sleeve -- USUALLY negative (-) / ground. 5.5 mm outer diameter (common)

variants: Center-positive (tip +) is the modern default; some older/vintage gear (and many guitar pedals) are center-negative. The barrel connector symbol on the device shows which pin the + goes to.
Inner diameter matters: a 2.1 mm plug in a 2.5 mm jack makes intermittent contact (loose center pin); they look identical but aren't interchangeable.
gotchas: Polarity is NOT standardized -- reversing center-positive vs center-negative can destroy the device. Check the symbol or meter the supply before plugging in an unknown wall-wart.
The center pin (2.1 vs 2.5 mm) and outer (5.5 mm typical, but 3.5/3.8/6.3 exist) must both match; wrong inner size = flaky power that browns out under load.
Barrel jacks have no keying and no make-before-break sequencing -- inserting a live plug can arc across the pins briefly; power the supply after connecting where you can.
notes: Coaxial DC barrel: center pin + outer sleeve, polarity by convention (center-positive typical). Common 5.5mm OD / 2.1mm ID size called out.
